title: Starship Flies to Orbit, but Its Booster Is Lost
summary:
On Friday, SpaceX's giant Starship rocket flew into orbit in its boldest test yet, but the first part of the plan went wrong.

SpaceX wanted to catch the whole rocket at its Texas launch pad. Big arms on the launch tower were meant to grab the booster as it came back down, then the spacecraft too. No one has ever caught a whole rocket this way.

The booster, called Super Heavy, is 236 feet tall. Soon after takeoff, it broke down and fell into the Gulf of Mexico. SpaceX had caught three boosters before, but this was the first try with the new, taller one.

The spacecraft kept flying. It is 171 feet tall. It reached orbit, ready to drop off 26 Starlink satellites. It will circle Earth 15 times, then try to come back to the pad on Saturday. Together they are 407 feet tall, the biggest and most powerful rocket in the world.

Catching the whole rocket could make space trips cheaper and more common, and SpaceX wants to use Starship for moon bases and trips to Mars.
why_it_matters: If rockets can be caught and reused, space trips get cheaper, and one day people like you might fly to space on one.
